## Git Worktrees for Multi-Agent Parallel Execution

### Core Concept
Git worktrees are ESSENTIAL for true parallel agent execution. Without worktrees, agents conflict and must run sequentially. With worktrees, all 15 agents can work simultaneously.

### Implementation Architecture
```
/home/opsvi/master_root/           # Main repository
/home/opsvi/agent_worktrees/       # Isolated agent workspaces
    ├── agent_1_requirements/      # Full repo copy for agent 1
    ├── agent_2_business/          # Full repo copy for agent 2
    └── ...up to 15 agents
/home/opsvi/agent_shared/          # Shared communication space
    ├── messages/                  # Inter-agent messaging
    ├── outputs/                   # Collected results
    └── metrics/                   # Performance tracking
```

Have 2 agents (requirements-analyst and business-analyst) collaboratively design requirements for their own inter-agent communication system. This is meta - agents designing the system they'll use to communicate.

### Test Results

- Score: 100/100
- Execution time: 2.0 seconds
- True parallel execution achieved (2.0s overlap)
- Messages exchanged: 1
- Both agents produced outputs

- Define functional requirements
- Define technical requirements  
- Define performance requirements
- Define security requirements
- Output: requirements_functional.md
